title: Baby and toddler storytime
summary: Songs, rhymes and two short books for babies and toddlers up to age three, with a grown-up.
body: Twenty-five minutes of songs, finger plays and board books, then free play with the soft blocks. Strollers can be parked by the story steps.

title: Tech help desk
summary: One-to-one help with phones, e-mail, printing, forms and the library apps.
body: Bring your device and your question. Staff can help with setting up e-books, printing a boarding pass, scanning a document or attaching a file. Staff do not repair devices.

title: Makerspace open hours
summary: 3D printers, a laser cutter, sewing machines and a vinyl cutter, with staff on hand.
body: New makers do a 10-minute safety walk-through first. Prints under 4 hours are free; bring your own design or pick one from the binder.

title: Preschool storytime
summary: Stories, songs and a small craft for ages three to five.
body: Each week has a theme. In November: weather, wheels, and things that grow.

title: Ledger Room hours: family history
summary: Find a great-grandparent in the Ossingford Ledger, the city directories or the county marriage index.
body: A local history librarian helps you start a search and use the microfilm readers. Bring names, rough dates and any places you know.

title: Teen game night
summary: Board games, card games and the Switch, for grades 6 to 12.
body: Snacks on the first Tuesday of the month. Game of the month: a cooperative one.

title: Wednesday morning book club
summary: A long-running club that reads one novel a month and talks about it over coffee.
body: November: The Weir Keeper by Lina Hargrove (fictional). Copies are held at the Central desk for club members to borrow.

title: English conversation circle
summary: Practice everyday English with neighbors and a volunteer facilitator. All levels.
body: No homework and no sign-up. Topics this month: the doctor's office, the bus, and talking to a child's teacher.

title: Lego lab
summary: A big table of bricks and a weekly building challenge for ages five to eleven.
body: Finished builds are displayed by the front desk for a week.

title: Seed library swap
summary: Take seeds, bring seeds, and ask the master gardeners what to plant in late fall.
body: The seed library lives in the old oak card catalog. Garlic and spring bulbs are the swap focus in November.

title: Friday film: classics on the big screen
summary: A classic film in the meeting room, with captions on and a short introduction.
body: This month's films are all set on rivers. The list is at the desk.

title: Podcast booth basics
summary: Learn the recording booth in 45 minutes: mics, levels, and exporting your file.
body: After the session you can use the booth on your own whenever it is free.

title: Saturday family storytime
summary: Stories for the whole family on the weekend, with a different reader each week.
body: Guest readers this month include the county fire chief and a children's author (both fictional).

title: Author talk: writing about a river town
summary: Lina Hargrove (fictional) on researching The Weir Keeper in the Ledger Room.
body: A 40-minute talk and questions. Copies of the book can be borrowed at the Central desk.

title: Bookmobile at the Saturday market
summary: Library cards, holds pickup and new picture books at the farmers market.
body: The Bookmobile parks at the north side of the square, next to the cider stand.

title: Sunday knitting circle
summary: Bring a project, any craft with yarn. Needles to borrow from the Library of Things.
body: Beginners welcome. Volunteers can teach a cast-on and a knit stitch.
